newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Explosive find under Belgian retirement home.
newsitem.headline: Explosive find under Belgian retirement home.

text.p: Belgian police cleared a pensioners' home in a Brussels suburb after they found a cache of 40 kg of explosives, rifles and ammunition in a garage underneath the institution.
The Brussels public prosecutor confirmed the find on Friday and told local media he was following "serious leads" in the case, which prevented him from disclosing details.
The arms were found on Thursday by the owner of the garage, one of several underneath The Maples retirement home in the Brussels suburb of Uccle.
He become suspicious after the person renting the garage had been out of contact for months, Belgian television said.
Some of the explosives were leaking and police called in the bomb disposal squad and evacuated pensioners to the local town hall's wedding room while the explosives and guns were removed.

Belgian media speculated the arms belonged either to leftwing urban guerillas, who carried out attacks in Belgium in the 1980s, or to gangs of criminals who have recently been robbing security vans and blowing up bank cash machines.
A Belgian police arms specialist told Belgian radio the arms mostly likely originated on the black market or could have come from surplus stocks in eastern Europe.
